title: composite-sli-and-priority-error-budget-policy-for-heterogeneous-endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a composable SLI taxonomy and a prioritized error budget policy for heterogeneous model endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, reranking). The goal is to: (1) specify SLIs per endpoint and per model-variant that capture user-perceived correctness/latency/availability, (2) create composite SLIs for multi-route operations, (3) define error budget burn tiers and automated mitigations (circuit breakers, selective failover, and tiered load shedding), and (4) produce an ops-ready playbook + observability dashboards for rollout and incident response.
slis: latency_p95_ms: p95 response time for non-streaming endpoints (exclude client-cancelled)
latency_p99_stream_ms: p99 per-chunk latency for streaming sessions (chat)
quality_regression_rate: percent of responses failing benchmark prompt set (monthly eval)
token_truncation_rate: percent of responses cut short due to token limit
embedding_similarity_consistency: % of embeddings within baseline cosine distance for canonical inputs
composite_request_success: AND over dependent routes (e.g., prompt-preprocess -> model -> postprocess)
sli_definition_notes: SLIs must be computed at route+model+region cardinality (e.g., chat.v1.us-west-2) to allow fine-grained attribution
For streaming endpoints, compute chunk-level latency and session-level availability separately
Quality SLI uses a daily sampled evaluation set plus canary/rollback prompts for immediate regressions
Exclude scheduled maintenance windows and customer-initiated cancellations from availability SLI calculations
error_budget_policy: Objective: Composite SLO = 99.9% availability (monthly) for Tier 1 customers; Tier 2: 99.7%; Tier 3: 99.0%
Error budget units = % of request failures + normalized quality-regression impact (weighted factor 2x for quality failures)

Burn tiers: Green (<30% burn) - no action; Amber (30-70%) - throttle non-critical background jobs, notify owners; Red (>70%) - enable circuit breakers & initiate failover runbook; Critical (>90%) - emergency scale and executive alert
Budget borrowing: allowed across models within same customer with explicit approval; borrowing requires a repayment plan within the next 14 days
Automatic enforcement hooks: policy engine will trigger actions when moving between tiers (see circuit-breaker and failover entries)
Rollbacks: any deploy that increases composite error budget burn by >5% within 1 hour should be auto-rolled back per rollout policy
circuit_breaker_policy: Per-route CB thresholds (evaluated on 1-minute and 5-minute windows):
- 5xx_rate > 2.0% sustained for 5m => open CB for that route-model-region pair
- p95_latency > target_latency*3 for 3 consecutive 1m windows => open CB
- queue_length > configured_capacity*0.6 continuously for 10m => open CB
Actions when CB opens: immediate fail-fast with HTTP 503 + 'try again later' header, fallback to degraded model variant if available, notify on-call, escalate error budget burn one tier
CB gradual recovery: half-open testing: allow 1% of pre-failure traffic as probe; if probes pass for 2 consecutive 1m windows, transition to closed and ramp traffic 2x per minute
Stability overrides: emergency hold by SRE lead to keep CB open during external incidents
multi_region_failover_policy: Primary/secondary routing: by default route to customer-preferred region; when region composite error budget burn > 70% or regional outage detected, fail traffic to nearest warm-standby region
Warm-standby requirements: at least 1 compatible GPU pool with pinned model variant and KV cache pre-warm window of 10 minutes
Cost-aware routing: prefer regional failover order configured per-customer (latency-first vs cost-first), with max cross-region traffic cap to avoid bill shock
Stateful session handling: for long-running chat sessions, attempt state migration via encrypted KV sync; if unavailable, continue in degraded mode with user-facing message
Failover testing: automated quarterly chaos exercises and canary failover drills recorded in console dashboards
load_shedding_policy: - Tier A (SLA-backed) = no shedding unless critical (>90% burn)
- Tier B (paid) = prefer degrade to smaller model variants, limit burst concurrency
- Tier C (free/experimental) = preemptable; subject to token-rate caps and early truncation

Shedding strategies (in order of preference): prefetched KV/cached response serve, reduce model size (downgrade to quantized variant), partial response (shorter max tokens), reject best-effort jobs (background/async), reject new sessions when queue > threshold
Graceful client contract: clients must handle 206 (partial) and 429/503 with Retry-After. SDKs will expose hints for expected degradation behavior
Telemetry: every shed decision emits a structured event with reason, affected customers, error budget delta, and mitigation taken
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-route/model/region SLI heatmap, rolling error budget burn chart, CB open-state board, failover events timeline
Alerts: Pager duty for Red+Critical burn tiers; Slack channel for Amber with context; automated tickets for persistent CB openings
SLO report cadence: weekly digest per product and daily during incident windows
Synthetic canaries: cold-start and warm-start synthetic transactions per region every 5m; compare against baseline and surface drift
rollout_and_validation: Phased rollout: dev -> canary (1% traffic, 30m) -> regional ramp (10%, 1h) -> global ramp (50%, 4h) with automated SLI guardrails
Canary success criteria: no >2% increase in error budget burn and no >5% increase in latency p95 in canary window
Post-deploy validation: automatic daily quality eval on golden prompts for 7 days to catch regressions
Runbook snippets: immediate steps for CB opening, regional failover initiation checklist, and steps for controlled load shedding
